title: Stone Credholm Platform Review 2026: Legit or Scam?
description: Stone Credholm platform review: what its site says about FCA status, deposits and automation, and the details to check before you sign up.
author: Olivia Bennett
excerpt: Stone Credholm platform says it is FCA-regulated, and its performance figures come with no stated method.
content:
Stone Credholm platform presents itself as a UK trading platform with fast trade routing, risk limits and a 24/7 support claim. Its site says it is FCA-regulated and shows a "Regulated" badge. This review separates what the site says from what can be checked.

The figures on the site (signal accuracy, uptime, traded volume and ratings) come with no method, period or definition, so we treat them as the platform's own statements.

Stone Credholm platform at a Glance

Here is what the site states and what it leaves out.

CategoryWhat the site says
Platform typeTrading platform with routed orders and risk limits
JurisdictionUK implied (GBP pricing, UK testimonials)
Minimum depositGBP 250 standard for UK users in our review. The site states £190
FeesSaid to be shown before you agree. No schedule on the page
Payment methodsVisa, Mastercard, PayPal, Apple Pay, Google Pay, bank transfer, SEPA and USDT
WithdrawalsBack to the original payment method, no timescale given
SupportDescribed as 24/7 in one place and weekday hours in the FAQ
Mobile appResponsive web only. No native app mentioned
Regulator or licenceFCA-regulated, per the site

Items marked as stated come from the platform's own site. We have not tested the platform.

The Main Claims, and What We Could Check

Regulation

The site says it is FCA-regulated, and a badge says the same. Before any deposit, search the FCA register for the operating company to confirm this.

Automation

The site describes instant trade routing with automatic exits when risk limits are breached. Other passages say a human analyst approves orders and that clients review recommendations before acting. These two descriptions do not match, so it is unclear how much trading happens without a person.

Performance and usage figures

The site cites signal accuracy of up to 85%, 99.3% signal uptime, £4.8 billion traded, around 31,900 active users and a 4.9 rating from 847 reviews. It gives no definition, time period or method for any of these. The user counts also differ between two places on the site.

Costs Worth Knowing

For UK users our standard minimum for this review is GBP 250. The platform's own site states £190, and that difference should be settled in the terms before any money moves. The site also says there are no hidden fees, but no fee schedule appears on the page, and the linked pricing page is not included in the content we reviewed.

Our standard minimum deposit for this review is 250 in the reader's local currency: AUD 250 in Australia, GBP 250 in the UK and EUR 250 in the EU. Where the platform states a different figure, we show it alongside ours. Confirm the exact amount in its terms before you deposit.

Who Is Behind the Brand

Its risk warning is present and states that capital is at risk. Before you deposit, confirm which company holds your money and who handles complaints.

Before You Register: A Short Checklist

  • Check the FCA register for the company that runs the platform.
  • Confirm the minimum deposit in the platform's own terms, since the site states £190 and this review uses GBP 250.
  • Get the full pricing schedule and withdrawal timescale in writing.
  • Find out whether a human analyst approves your trades before you rely on automation.

Risks to Keep in Mind

The main risk is relying on the FCA claim without checking it on the register. The second is the mix of automated and analyst-approved descriptions, which changes who is responsible for a trade. Market losses are possible, as the site's own warning confirms.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the minimum deposit for Stone Credholm platform?

For UK users our standard minimum for this review is GBP 250. The platform's own site states £190, so confirm the exact figure in its terms before depositing.

Is Stone Credholm platform FCA-regulated?

The site says it is FCA-regulated. Search the FCA register for the operating company before you register.

Does Stone Credholm platform charge fees?

The site says all charges are shown before you agree, but no fee schedule is published on the page. Read the full pricing terms first.

Does automation remove the risk of losing money?

No. The site itself says capital is at risk and losses are possible, and its description of how much trading is automated is unclear.

Our Verdict on Stone Credholm platform

The site says it is FCA-regulated, and its performance figures come with no stated method. Our rating reflects these gaps. We will revisit it once its FCA status is confirmed on the register. Start only with money you can afford to lose.
